scope: Independent read-only source review and CPU tokenizer audit; no training, GPU, network, chain or owner-source edits
training_findings: The exact selected set contains 749 training originals (42,290 whitespace words), 86 validation originals and 84 test originals.
No selected group, normalized full document or 12-word span crosses splits. This is evidence for the present snapshot, not a generic guarantee for future input paths.
Maximum BPE length with both real EOS tokens is 119 for train and 89 for validation/test. Default 256 truncates no selected document.
Causal language-model shifting is performed by the native GPT-2 model. Masking by attention_mask, rather than token ID, correctly retains real EOS targets even when EOS is used for padding.
Top-four-block adaptation leaves tied embedding/output weights and lower eight blocks frozen, while training final normalization and the last four blocks.
Validation contains no training rows; the best checkpoint is saved only after a validation improvement. The test set is read for group checks/provenance, not loss or optimizer updates.
Two epochs expose only about 97,344 BPE input tokens. This is a bounded voice adaptation of a pretrained teacher, not training a 124M model from scratch.
The CPU six-token smoke and a valid training objective do not establish prose quality. Its sample already changed a brass key into a silver key.

before_bulk_generation.finding: The current natural-ending filter scans prompt plus continuation and can accept the prompt alone.
before_bulk_generation.evidence: audit.json includes a 48-word prompt plus three unfinished generated words that passes the length filter unchanged.
before_bulk_generation.recommendation: Require at least one natural ending occurring after the prompt boundary and a minimum amount of retained generated prose; preserve raw text and rejection counts.

before_bulk_generation.finding: Prompt token length is unchecked and generation has no explicit native-context guard.
before_bulk_generation.recommendation: Before generation, assert each BOS-plus-prompt token count plus max_new does not exceed the model's native context size. Do not silently truncate factual prompt setup.

before_bulk_generation.finding: Checkpoint and prompt paths appear in the generation report, but immutable contents and prompt ancestry are not bound.
before_bulk_generation.recommendation: Record model/tokenizer/config/prompt SHA256 and source group IDs. Use only training-derived or new generation prompts for student data. Keep all siblings from a prompt/group together; keep evaluation prefixes and their outputs entirely excluded.

before_bulk_generation.finding: Training begins each document with EOS/BOS while sampling currently tokenizes only the prose prompt.
before_bulk_generation.recommendation: Use the same single native EOS/BOS initialization for both the base and adapted teacher comparison and for accepted bulk generation. This changes conditioning, not generated prose.

before_bulk_generation.finding: Positive batch/budget arguments are not all checked and final candidate count may overshoot by up to batch-1.
before_bulk_generation.recommendation: Reject nonpositive batch, target_tokens, max_candidates, eval_every and learning rate; clip the last candidate batch to its remaining limit.

evaluation.compare: original pretrained teacher versus validation-best adaptation, same prompts, decoding, seed order and batch size
evaluation.bulk_step: Only after manual raw-prose and training-copy review; accepted-length filters alone are insufficient
evaluation.final_test: Use untouched test-group prefixes only after teacher selection; never turn their continuations into student training material

limitations: The source set is small and stylistically repetitive; adapting the top four blocks may overfit it.

Independent document EOS supervision is appropriate for a paragraph teacher; it does not make the future stateful student continuous. Student training must still carry history and be tested without silent resets.
Teacher no-repeat and repetition-penalty settings are disclosed offline decoding choices. They are not part of the eventual on-chain student's neural runtime.
Absence of long exact training overlap does not prove originality or semantic novelty.
